text: In which Argyll forest were beavers officially released in 2009, the first wild ones in Britain for 400 years?
info: Knapdale Forest, in mid-Argyll between Lochgilphead and the Sound of Jura.

text: Onto which small Hebridean island were white-tailed eagles first released in 1975?
info: Rum, in the Small Isles south of Skye.

text: Where were European bison let loose in 2022, in woods just outside Canterbury?
info: West Blean and Thornden Woods, north of Canterbury in Kent.

text: Which island's capital, St Helier, was Jim Bergerac's patch?
info: Jersey, the largest Channel Island, off the coast of Normandy.

text: Which Glasgow district gave its name to the CID in Taggart?
info: Maryhill, in the north-west of Glasgow.

text: Which island off Amble is home to England's only colony of roseate terns?
info: Coquet Island, an RSPB reserve a mile off Amble.

text: Which village at the river's mouth has a ruined priory and castle on its headland and the Longsands beach?
info: Tynemouth, on the north side of the mouth of the Tyne.

text: Which sea stack off South Shields had a staircase cut into it, with a pub in a cave in the cliffs nearby?
info: Marsden Rock, in Marsden Bay; the Marsden Grotto pub is cut into the cliff.
